summary_html: CPS **screens out** a report (no investigation) or closes as **unfounded** after minimal review. Federal law (CAPTA) conditions funding on operating screening criteria and recordkeeping; federal reviews (CFSR) assess decision quality.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — screening & intake system requirements  
- **CFSR Regulations (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal performance/quality review of state screening and responses

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: S.C. v. New Jersey Department of Children and Families
key_cases.holding: The Court upheld the Department's 'not established' investigative category but required improved notice, a credible-evidence basis, and an informal opportunity to respond, while rejecting any right to a contested OAL hearing.
key_cases.relevance: S.C. governs the consequences of closing an investigation short of substantiation, including non-expungement of the record.
key_cases.quote: We reject that due process considerations require the Department to conduct an adjudicative contested case proceeding either internally or at the Office of Administrative Law for a "not established" finding.

key_cases.case_name: N.J. Department of Children & Families v. R.R.
key_cases.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
key_cases.holding: The court reversed a 'not established' finding as unsupported by the record and directed that the allegation be deemed 'unfounded' so the records would be treated accordingly.
key_cases.relevance: R.R. shows that even a closure short of substantiation must have record support or be converted to 'unfounded' and expunged.
key_cases.quote: As we find that the Division erred in finding the allegation was "not established," the Division shall deem the allegation to be "unfounded" and treat the records accordingly.

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Division of Youth & Family Services v. P.W.R.
key_cases.holding: The Court reversed the abuse-or-neglect finding, holding the record inadequate to establish a Title 9 violation and that an occasional slap to a teenager's face as discipline, causing no bruising or marks, is not 'excessive corporal punishment' under N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.21(c)(4)(b).
key_cases.relevance: P.W.R. shows that conduct the Division itself labelled 'unfounded' cannot later be converted into a finding of physical abuse.
key_cases.quote: Limiting state involvement only to interference with excessive corporal punishment requires the exercise of judgment by reviewing courts before a finding of physical abuse is entered against a parent.

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediately upon receipt of the report; investigation initiated within 24 hours
timeline_requirements.starts_from: The Division's receipt of a report of child abuse or neglect
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.11; a delay in initiating the investigation is permitted only where the Division or other designated entity authorizes it at the request of a law enforcement official.

timeline_requirements.starts_from: State Central Registry assigns the CPS report to the local office for response
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Good cause must be established and an extension approved by the local office manager or designee before day 60 (CP&P-II-C-6-200).
